prompt: Write an email to a colleague about a new hobby you have taken up. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: I've taken up pottery (and I'm hooked)

Hi Sam,

I hope your week is going well. I wanted to share something a little outside the usual work chatter: I've started taking pottery classes, and I can't stop thinking about it.

It began in August, when my partner gave me a gift certificate for a beginner wheel-throwing course at a studio near my apartment. I'll admit I went in skeptical. I spend my days in spreadsheets and documents, and I wasn't sure I had the patience or the coordination for clay. The first night, I spent forty-five minutes trying to center a single lump on the wheel, and it kept wobbling off to one side like it had a mind of its own. My instructor, a very calm woman named Dana, told me that nearly everyone struggles with centering at first and that it's really a lesson in letting go of control. I laughed, but she's right.

Eight weeks in, I can now produce something that resembles a bowl. It's lopsided, a bit thick at the bottom, and I wouldn't serve soup in it, but it's mine, and I'm weirdly proud of it. Last week I finally pulled up a small cylinder with straight walls, and I may have celebrated more than the moment deserved. The class applauded, which didn't help my humility.

What I enjoy most is how absorbing it is. When my hands are in the clay, I'm not checking email or running through my to-do list. There's just the wheel, the water, and the feel of the clay shifting under my fingers. I walk out of the studio feeling calmer than when I walked in, even with clay under my fingernails and splashed up to my elbows. It's become the best part of my Tuesday evenings.

There's also something satisfying about making a physical object after so much work that lives on a screen. Mistakes are visible, but they're also forgiving. You can slice a collapsed pot in half, learn why it fell, and reclaim the clay to try again. I could stand to take that attitude into my project work, honestly.

My next challenge is glazing. I have a few pieces waiting to be fired, and I have no idea how they'll turn out, since the colors change so much in the kiln. I'll bring in whatever survives. Consider yourself warned: you may end up with a slightly crooked mug on your desk.

If you've ever been curious, the studio runs a free open house on the first Saturday of the month, and I'd be happy to go along. Do you have any hobbies you've picked up lately? I'd love to hear about them.

Best,
[name]
